title: After years of blowing accounts, I took myself out of my own trading. It was the only thing that worked.
author: FossilBlade
selftext:
Been trading futures for years, mostly MNQ. And for most of those years my problem was never the setups — it was me. Moved stops, cut winners early, revenge-traded after red days, oversized when I was "sure." I could backtest something solid and then fumble it live every time. Sound familiar?  
  
  
About a year ago I stopped trying to fix my psychology and just took myself out of the loop — fully automated, runs on NinjaTrader, I don't touch it.  
  
  
I'm keeping the specifics to myself, but there's no secret sauce to how it behaves — the character of it is simple enough:  
  
  
\- It's active. Twenty-odd small, rule-based trades a session, not one or two big swings I agonise over.  
\- Fixed risk per trade — same size, same process, every single time, zero "feel."  
\- Every exit is by rule. It trails the stop and never grabs a profit early just because I'd be tempted to.  
\- A hard daily loss cap and a forced flatten, so one ugly session can't bury a good week.  
\- Set up once, then hands-off. That was the entire point.  
  
  
The dumb truth is the edge isn't a magic indicator — it's that the software doesn't panic and I do. Removing myself is what finally turned the curve up and to the right.  
  
  
I didn't trust it on vibes. \~7 years of backtest first — every single year green, including 2020 and 2022 — then through prop evaluations. Attaching the full backtest, the 50K evaluation report, and my actual Lucid payout + calendar so it's not just numbers in a vacuum.  
  
  
If you're heading down the automation road, happy to discuss further on how to make it better.
